te.title: Product off-spec with a good-looking wash front
te.sit: The laboratory reports the last PX product sample at 97.4 % and falling. On the DCS ZI-107 sits on its 50 % set point, PI-105 is normal and the product flow looks high.

te.title: Reject PX creeping up at night
te.sit: The isomerization unit says the reject PX content is higher than usual. TIC-310 is on AUTO at its −29 °C set point but TI-310 has been a little warm for an hour. PI-501 has been in alarm and was acknowledged.

te.title: Wash column pressure climbing
te.sit: Over the last half hour PI-105 has risen from 6 to almost 10 bar g. The product flow and purity are normal. The feed, TIC-110 and DIC-115 have not been touched.

te.title: Melt drum emptying
te.sit: LI-401 has fallen from 60 to under 40 % in half an hour and LIC-401 is cutting the melt return. V-202 level LI-213 looks normal at 60 %.

te.title: Scraper current creeping up on E-201
te.sit: JI-206 reads 85 A, up from its normal 75 A. TIC-210 is on set point and the jacket TI-212 is colder than usual. The product is fine.

te.title: Wet cake from the recovery centrifuge
te.sit: The melt drum AI-404 has fallen from 91 to 87 % and LI-401 is rising. AI-324 is in alarm. The C-304 motor current is 140 A (normal 112 A).

te.title: Warm purity stage
te.sit: TI-403 is in LO alarm at 11 °C with TV-403 at 100 %. The operator on the purity stage says PIC-111 is running at a higher pressure than usual and the crystals look bigger.

te.title: Stage 3 too cold but reject too lean
te.sit: TI-310 has been in HI alarm, yet the reject PX AI-324 is 26 %, lower than normal, and JI-306 is at 77 A.

te.title: Melt drum filling with the return valve wide open
te.sit: LI-401 is at 70 % and climbing. FIC-402 is in CAS with its output at 100 %, yet FI-402 has not moved from 110.6 t/h in half an hour.

te.title: Wash column stopped on high pressure
te.sit: The wash column tripped on PSHH-105 a few minutes ago. Before the trip TI-109 had been in LO alarm for 20 minutes with TV-109 at 100 %, and the product flow had fallen to about 3 t/h.

te.title: V-202 draw thick after a short stop
te.sit: Two minutes ago the scraper M-201 current jumped above 95 A and XV-218 closed. The scraper itself was not touched. DI-215 is in HI alarm.

te.title: Reject flow cut in half
te.sit: FI-322 dropped from 34 to about 11 t/h and has been recovering slowly. LI-313 is rising and C-304 is drawing more current. Nothing was changed on the unit.

meta.title: Troubleshooting report — TE-3 Wash column pressure climbing (PX Melt Crystallizer)
meta.sit: Over the last half hour PI-105 has risen from 6 to almost 10 bar g. The product flow and purity are normal. The feed, TIC-110 and DIC-115 have not been touched.

0.1.unit: Three-stage suspension melt crystallization. 40 t/h of mixed xylenes (40 wt% PX) are cooled in three scraped-surface crystallizers E-101/201/301 with growth vessels V-102/202/302 at 3, −4 and −29 °C. Stage-1 slurry goes to the hydraulic wash column W-104, which presses the crystals into a packed bed, washes it with its own melt and sends 6.2 t/h PX at 99.9 wt% (FI-108, AI-120); the filtrate goes back to stage 2. Stages 2 and 3 are separated by the centrifuges C-204/C-304; their cake is melted in V-401 and returned to V-102. K-501 supplies the propylene refrigerant.

rows.what: PI-105 climbing from 6 to almost 10 bar g over half an hour
Product flow and purity look normal
Feed, TIC-110 and DIC-115 have not been touched

0.4.ctx: Unit lined out at design at 00:00; no work permits open on the unit; fractionation steady.

R.1.p: The wash column filters the slurry through a packed bed of PX crystals. The hydraulic pressure PI-105 is the force needed to push the liquid through that bed. A packed bed resists flow according to Kozeny–Carman: the pressure drop grows with the liquid flow and its viscosity and falls with the square of the particle size. Smaller crystals → many more, narrower channels → much more resistance. Crystal size is set upstream, in V-102: growth against nucleation, and breakage by the agitator (attrition).

Crystal size (AI-116 mean size, design 250 µm)
Fitted: piston and screen part a, bed part b at 250 µm

TOP: PI-105 rising toward the W-104 trip

   OR — More viscous liquid (cold melt loop)

6.3.fut: A packed-bed wash column is only as good as the crystals it gets: protect the crystal size upstream.

6.4.how: A W-104 trip avoided: a trip with a full, fine bed means emptying and rebuilding it, taken as 16 h without product at 6.19 t/h and USD 370/t (OTS prices; the 16 h is assumed)

PI-105 rose 5.99 → 9.63 bar g in 30 min; first above 6.5 at 00:07:30; still rising 0.10 bar/min at 00:30.

evidence.text: Lab 00:32: product 99.879 wt% PX; crystals under the microscope: stage 1 177 µm with many fragments, stage 2 220 µm, stage 3 160 µm; C-304 cake 0.20 kg liquid/kg crystals; melt 91.2 wt% PX.
Two-point fit of the run: PI-105 ≈ 1.96 + 4.03·(250/L)² bar g. The bed term grows as 1/L², as Kozeny–Carman says for a finer packed bed.
T-2: feed 40 → 34 t/h at 00:35: PI-105 10.04 → 9.10 bar g at 00:55 although AI-116 kept falling 177 → 165 µm.

hyp.cause: Crystal attrition in V-102: a damaged M-102 impeller breaks crystals into fragments
hyp.cat: Feed & crystallization stages (FIC-101, V-102/202/302, E-101/201/301, scrapers, agitators)
hyp.ifthen: If the impeller breaks crystals, AI-116 falls first, then PI-105 rises as the finer bed packs tighter; stage 2 and 3 sizes stay put; the lab sees fragments; the bed law follows 1/L²; once the impeller is repaired the size and PI-105 come back
hyp.key: AI-116 ↓ before PI-105 ↑; fragments under the microscope; PI-105 follows (250/L)²
hyp.fals: AI-116 steady, or no fragments, or PI-105 stays high after the size has recovered

hyp.cause: Melt loop too cold: unmelted crystals and viscous liquid in the W-104 bed (TIC-109, E-105 steam)
hyp.cat: Wash column W-104 & melt loop (PI-105, ZIC-107, E-105, FV-108, AI-120)
hyp.ifthen: If the melt loop is cold, TI-109 is below 18 °C and TIC-109 OUT high; the crystal size upstream does not change

hyp.cause: More crystals sent to W-104: V-102 colder or DIC-115 asking for more solids
hyp.cat: Feed & crystallization stages (FIC-101, V-102/202/302, E-101/201/301, scrapers, agitators)
hyp.ifthen: If the solids load rises, DI-115 rises above 4.1 wt% and TI-110 falls; FI-108 rises with it

hyp.cause: PT-105A drifting high (the pressure is not really rising)
hyp.ifthen: If the transmitter drifts, the local reading at W-104 disagrees with PI-105 and nothing else moves; a load change does not move the reading
hyp.key: Local reading ≠ PI-105; PI-105 deaf to the load
hyp.fals: Local reading agrees and PI-105 follows the load

hyp.cat: Wash column W-104 & melt loop (PI-105, ZIC-107, E-105, FV-108, AI-120)
hyp.ifthen: If the screen blocks, PI-105 rises and the filtrate FI-122 falls at the same feed, whatever the crystal size; repairing stage 1 changes nothing
hyp.key: FI-122 ↓ with PI-105 ↑; no link to AI-116
hyp.fals: FI-122 steady and PI-105 follows AI-116 back down

hyp.cause: Fines from a nucleation burst on the E-101 wall (jacket too cold, scraper not clearing)
hyp.cat: Refrigeration & utilities (K-501 C3=, PIC-111/211/311, steam, air, power)
hyp.ifthen: If the wall nucleates, the jacket TI-112 is colder than −3 °C or JI-106 rises with scale; PIC-111 OUT moves
hyp.fals: TI-112, PI-111 and JI-106 on design

hyp.cause: Feed change from fractionation (PX content, temperature or an impurity)
hyp.ifthen: If the feed changed, AI-103 or TI-102 moves, and all three stages would feel it
hyp.key: AI-103 / TI-102 move; AI-216 and AI-316 move too
hyp.fals: AI-103 and TI-102 on design; only stage 1 affected
